do_not_reward: degrees, MBA, college or employer prestige
feature or output counts with no adoption or outcome attached

criteria.name: Lived freight / logistics operations experience
criteria.measures: Has personally done the operational work in freight forwarding, customs/CHA, port, documentation or 3PL carrier operations. Not sold to it, built for it, or read about it.

anchors.2: adjacent (e-commerce fulfilment, or built software for / sold into logistics) or under 1 yr hands-on
anchors.4: 2+ yrs hands-on in freight forwarding / customs / port / 3PL carrier ops, with named specifics (documents, carriers, ports, exceptions)

criteria.hire_evidence: Rohan, Sunita, Aditya, Meghna, Lavanya (all Exceeds). Vikram, Rahul, Preetham have none.
criteria.probe: Walk me through a shipment that went wrong and what you did.

criteria.name: Self-started fixes adopted beyond own remit
criteria.measures: Spotted an unowned problem, built the fix unasked, and others adopted it without a mandate.

anchors.2: built tools or processes, but used only within own team
anchors.4: built at least one thing unasked that was adopted by other teams, with a measurable effect

criteria.hire_evidence: Rohan (BoL tool), Sunita (weekend workflow redesign), Meghna (30-60-90 framework), Lavanya (dashboard, scorecard, triage).
criteria.probe: What did you build that nobody asked for? Who ended up using it?

criteria.name: Unmediated ownership of an outcome
criteria.measures: Sole or top owner of a product area or outcome, with no senior layer making the calls and no intermediary between them and users.

anchors.0: contributor inside a structured team with layers above
anchors.2: owns a module with some autonomy but a layer above sets direction
anchors.4: sole owner; made and lived with consequential calls; early-stage or rules-not-written environment

criteria.hire_evidence: Lavanya (sole PM), Rohan, Aditya, Meghna. Contrast: Vikram (4-PM team, CTO/VP sales layer), Preetham (1 of 12 engineers).
criteria.probe: Tell me about a call you made where nobody could overrule you.

criteria.name: Decisions from evidence: shipped, killed, learned, documented
criteria.measures: Ships and kills based on usage data or outcomes, and writes down why. Shipping volume alone does not count.

anchors.0: no evidence of measurement or of stopping anything
anchors.2: tracks metrics on shipped work, no evidence of killing or pivoting
anchors.4: killed or pivoted on data, documented the reasoning, outcome stated

criteria.hire_evidence: Lavanya (killed 2 features on usage data, wrote the outage post-mortem), Aditya (loss post-mortem, root cause documented).
criteria.probe: What did you kill, and what told you to?

criteria.name: Direct contact with the people who use the product
criteria.measures: Discovery straight with end users, unmediated by sales, CS or research teams.

anchors.2: structured research, or user contact mediated by others
anchors.4: repeated direct contact that led to a product change with a measured result

criteria.hire_evidence: Lavanya (3 parallel discovery tracks with forwarders), Meghna, Aditya.
criteria.probe: What did the last user you spoke to tell you that surprised you?

criteria.name: Lived freight / logistics operations experience
criteria.measures: Same definition and anchors as PM-1. Weighted slightly lower than for PM because SPM-2 separately covers technical depth. Preetham shows that integration knowledge from outside the domain does not substitute.

anchors.2: adjacent (e-commerce fulfilment, or built software for / sold into logistics) or under 1 yr hands-on
anchors.4: 2+ yrs hands-on in freight forwarding / customs / port / 3PL carrier ops, with named specifics (documents, carriers, ports, exceptions)

criteria.probe: Where in a forwarder's day do integrations break first?

criteria.name: Integration / platform / data-layer judgment
criteria.measures: Decisions about how a product connects to messy external systems (carriers, ports, ERP, customer tools), including what to build, configure, or stay away from.

anchors.2: worked with or contributed to integrations, did not own the decisions
anchors.4: owned build / buy / configure / avoid decisions on an integration or data layer, with consequences and results stated

criteria.hire_evidence: Rohan (led a vendor migration after finding reliability issues, 60% lower lag, no data loss), Lavanya (carrier integration work, first API docs, integration timelines cut by 2 weeks). Preetham has deep technical work but rates Below, so this is capped at 20.
criteria.probe: What did you decide not to integrate, and why?

criteria.name: Unmediated ownership with consequences
criteria.measures: Same definition as PM-3, at senior scope: owned a product area without senior PMs above, and lived with the outcome.

anchors.0: contributor inside a structured team with layers above
anchors.2: owns a module with some autonomy but a layer above sets direction
anchors.4: sole owner; made and lived with consequential calls; early-stage or rules-not-written environment

criteria.probe: Which decision of yours do you still live with today?

criteria.name: Builds the practices others adopt
criteria.measures: Created standards, frameworks or decision processes that outlasted them and were adopted without a mandate. The SPM JD asks the person to help define how the PM function works.

anchors.4: created a standard or framework from nothing that others adopted, with a measurable effect

criteria.hire_evidence: Meghna (30-60-90 framework), Sunita (SOPs adopted in full in 60 days), Rohan (code review and on-call, 40% fewer P1s), Lavanya (scorecard methodology, first API docs).
criteria.probe: What standard did you create that people still follow?

criteria.name: Reliability and root-cause ownership under pressure
criteria.measures: Finds the real cause of a systemic failure, fixes it fast, owns follow-up to closure.

anchors.0: no incident or quality ownership described
anchors.2: participated in incident response or quality work
anchors.4: led root-cause work on a systemic issue, fixed it, prevented recurrence, with results stated

criteria.hire_evidence: Rohan (root cause in 3 hrs, same-day fix), Sunita (pre-inspection audit found 4 gaps), Lavanya (outage post-mortem owned to closure). Preetham also shows this and rates Below, so it is weighted lower and not sufficient alone.
criteria.probe: Tell me about the worst data-quality failure you owned.
